title: A Simulation Framework for Workload Management in Hybrid Quantum-HPC Cloud System
problem: Hybrid quantum-HPC cloud platforms require workload management across classical and quantum resources, introducing challenges in device variability, noise-prone quantum processors, and distributed orchestration.
motivation: Develop simulation frameworks and taxonomy to guide workload management strategies in emerging hybrid quantum-HPC systems, enabling optimization under realistic constraints.
method: They developed HybridCloudSim, a simulation tool that models hybrid quantum-HPC cloud systems—environments where classical computers work alongside quantum computers to handle computational tasks. The tool lets researchers test different scheduling and resource allocation strategies (methods for deciding which tasks run on which computer and when) without needing actual hardware. They also surveyed existing scheduling and orchestration techniques and organized them by their underlying strategy, resource allocation approach, how they coordinate work across distributed systems, and the metrics they use to measure performance.
key_novelty: HybridCloudSim combines a survey of scheduling techniques with a simulation framework for hybrid quantum-HPC systems that models real-world challenges: quantum processor noise, device variability, and distributed coordination.
contributions: Comprehensive survey of workload management techniques in classical HPC, quantum clouds, and hybrid systems
Taxonomy categorizing approaches by scheduling strategy, allocation model, orchestration, and metrics
HybridCloudSim simulation framework for modeling hybrid quantum-HPC environments
Practical tool for optimizing resource usage under realistic constraints

metrics.primary: Resource utilization in hybrid quantum-HPC systems

limitations: Appears to be survey-focused with framework as secondary contribution. No specific performance evaluation results provided in abstract.
primary_theme: Workload Management in Hybrid Quantum-HPC Systems
